dedupe_keys.name: techno economic simulation results of egs based district heating in the northeastern united states nrel dgeo gdr

description: This dataset presents results of techno-economic simulations with the Distributed Geothermal Market Demand Model (dGeo), developed by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory, to evaluate the feasibility of Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) based district heating in the Northeastern United States. It was created in the Cornell EGS Ground-Truthing Project and gives census tract-level inputs and outputs: thermal demand, road length, energy prices, geothermal system sizing, annual energy from geothermal and natural gas peaking boilers, capital and operation and maintenance costs, and the levelized cost of heat. Key parameters include geothermal gradients, measured well depths, production temperatures and district heating piping lengths based on neighbourhood road lengths, with a target bottom hole temperature of 80 degrees C and new networks assumed in each census tract. Files are a simulation results workbook with a Parameter Key sheet and a 3.1 MB dGeo documentation report. Coverage is one U.S. region. Access: free download from the Geothermal Data Repository, DOI 10.15121/2507420. Caveats: modelled, not observed, results under fixed assumptions. It suits regional heat network feasibility studies, and relates to the GeoDH European layers catalogued here.
